title: Mouse Without Borders Portable 1.0.1-rc.8
summary: Settings cleanup with inline default labels, Installation controls, a selectable receiving folder, and optional automatic transfer-window closing. RC7 installer and transfer fixes are retained; existing supported preferences and protocol-2 recovery remain compatible.
changes: Group mouse, sharing/transfers, and shortcuts into measured, wrapping settings rows with clear default labels and explanations. Move DNS validation into IP Mappings.
Remove service-only controls and the misleading subnet checkbox. Disable optional clipboard/network status popups; keep actual failures and Mini Log. Explicit managed network policy remains enforced.

Clarify that Allow file transfers covers drag/drop and clipboard file copying. Preserve its saved choice when opening Settings or toggling Share Clipboard. Remove page flashing during preference saves.
Rename Portable to Installation. Move Start with Windows and Uninstall from the tray into that tab, alongside current paths, Open folder, and Install for me for portable copies.
Choose a default receiving folder on each PC for new drag/drop transfers. Explorer folder targets still take precedence. Unavailable custom folders fail clearly rather than redirecting files.
Add Automatically close finished transfers, enabled by default. Turning it off keeps finished/cancelled rows visible; explicit close still waits for cleanup and errors stay visible.

Preserve existing supported preferences, key, and layout. Add tests for migration, install copying, failed preference saves, unavailable destinations, settings layout, and automatic closing. Update documentation.
testing: Install RC8 over RC7 on both PCs. Check About, automatic launch, key/layout, and your existing supported checkbox/shortcut choices.
Open Other Options at your usual display scale, resize Settings, and scroll through all controls. Check defaults, explanations, dropdowns, and absence of service/subnet/status-message options.
Disable Allow file transfers, close/reopen Settings, then turn Share Clipboard off/on. The saved file-transfer choice must stay off. Re-enable it before transfer tests.

Choose a new receiving folder on the receiver. Drop to its desktop, then separately into an Explorer folder. Check the destination and immediate folder opening. Restart and verify the saved choice; Use default should restore Desktop/MouseWithoutBorders.
Choose a temporary custom folder, rename it, then drop to the desktop. Expect an error and no copy to another folder. Restore the folder or choose a valid destination afterward.

Turn automatic closing off on one PC. Complete or cancel transfers: its list should remain visible while the other PC follows its own setting. Turn it back on and check automatic closing. Closing active work still asks to cancel.

In Installation, toggle Start with Windows and reopen Settings to verify it. Check Open folder. If testing uninstall, use a disposable installation and choose No to keep preferences; Cancel must exit the uninstall flow.
Recheck ordinary mouse/keyboard/clipboard use, transfer pause/cancel/recovery, duplicate-name protection, and sleep/reconnect.
known_limitations: Real Windows Explorer, physical display scaling, startup/uninstall, and two-PC behavior still need the manual checks above; automated tests cannot replace them.

Receiving-folder and automatic-close preferences belong to each PC. Changing the folder affects new durable drag/drop transfers only; existing jobs and legacy clipboard file copying keep their prior destinations.

The receiving folder must be an accessible ordinary local directory. Linked directories and unavailable drives are rejected. No overwrite/merge, protocol, concurrency, speed, service, or automatic-update behavior is added.
Use the same RC on both PCs for consistent Settings. RC6/RC7 protocol-2 transfers remain compatible; older EXEs may discard the new preference fields if they rewrite the same preferences file.
Full-speed Wi-Fi transfers can still cause mouse lag. Offline temporary data can only be cleaned when the peer reconnects.
